stories.headline: Clippers indicate Chris Paul's old No. 3 going to Bradley Beal
stories.summary: Clippers guard Bradley Beal is take over the No. 3 jersey long associated with franchise legend Chris Paul, who has been recently outspoken about his treatment by the team.
stories.body:
LOS ANGELES -- LA Clippers guard Bradley Beal is expected to don the No. 3 jersey long associated with franchise legend Chris Paul during the 2026-27 NBA season.

Beal's new jersey number is available on the team's online store, and league sources told ESPN that Beal plans to wear No. 3.

Beal also appeared to address the situation in a social media post Thursday.

"He's a legend," Beal wrote. "The HISTORY and BRAND can't be touched, nor erased!!!"

Beal, 33, wore No. 3 for the first 13 seasons of his career with the Washington Wizards and Phoenix Suns before switching to No. 0 last season, his first with the Clippers, to accommodate Paul. Paul, 41, wore No. 3 for the Clippers from 2011 to 2017 and during his short-lived return to the franchise last season.

The Clippers initially gave No. 3 to Beal after signing him in the summer of 2025, but Clippers president Lawrence Frank said at the time that Beal offered the number back to Paul once he joined the roster.

After being sent home by the Clippers in December 2025, Paul announced his retirement in February after 21 seasons. Paul said in February that Frank told him that his No. 3 jersey would eventually be retired by the franchise.

Beal wearing No. 3 doesn't preclude the Clippers from honoring Paul with a jersey retirement in the future.

Paul was outspoken about his abrupt departure from the Clippers in an interview published last week, calling it "probably one of the most disrespectful things I've endured."

Long known as CP3, Paul is the Clippers' career leader in assists, led the franchise to the playoffs in six straight seasons and oversaw the "Lob City" era with Blake Griffin and DeAndre Jordan.

Beal, who was limited to six games last season due to injury, re-signed with the Clippers on a two-year, $13.2 million contract this summer.

stories.headline: Weekend predictions: Can Wrexham get a win? Who wins Manchester derby? Elversberg over Bayern?
stories.summary: Arsenal host Chelsea in a heavyweight clash this early in the Premier League, while teams such as PSG and Napoli are on the ropes in their respective title races.
stories.body:
Ahead of the latest weekend of European soccer, we pick out the must-watch matches from around the continent. We have the Manchester derby, two big-spending teams looking to get their first wins of the season, Jose Mourinho and the ultimate surprise package looking for the biggest victory in their history.

We are across the Premier League, Ligue 1, LaLiga, Bundesliga, Serie A and Women's Super League as we preview the weekend's action.

Is this Maresca's biggest test yet?

Manchester United vs. Manchester City

Premier League, Matchday 4

Kickoff: Sunday, 11.30 a.m. / 4.30 p.m. BST

Manchester City are bubbling nicely under new manager Enzo Maresca. Three wins from three in the league and a victory on the road in the Champions League midweek is a nice, immediate return after spending £326 million on a brand-new midfield.

This weekend will bring Maresca his first Manchester derby: a match where emotions can render form and reason obsolete -- then again, City's star striker, Erling Haaland, will have something to say about that. City's wins in the Premier League saw them leave it late to beat Bournemouth, hammer Crystal Palace and then battle through wastefulness and the odd dab of fortune to beat Coventry 1-0.

Haaland has been central to all, as has playmaker Rayan Cherki. But building an understanding in midfield are their new-look triumvirate of Elliot Anderson, Ayyoub Bouaddi and Enzo Fernández. It cost a fortune, but they are already showing their worth (Bouaddi, especially, was outstanding against FC Porto in the Champions League this week.) But how will that midfield withstand their biggest test yet?

United's season has started in underwhelming fashion: a loss to Hull, a big win over Ipswich and then a draw with Everton in which they conceded a 96th minute equalizer. They've also had two days' fewer rest, after playing Sabah in their Champions League opener on Thursday evening.

United need a statement win to kickstart their season, City will be looking for a result as further proof of the ease at which they're settling into life under Maresca.

MY PREDICTION: Man United 1-2 Man City. Form says City should win. United will need to put in their best performance of the season to stop them, but will I expect them to fall short.

Can Elversberg achieve the ultimate 'David vs. Goliath' upset?

Elversberg vs. Bayern Munich

Bundesliga, Matchday 3

Kickoff: Sunday, 11.30 a.m. / 5.30 p.m. CEST

The money Elversberg have spent on transfers in their entire history totals about €12 million. That's about a quarter of what defending champions Bayern Munich spent to bring in Nathaniel Brown in the summer from Eintracht Frankfurt.

You'd imagine the two sides will be at the opposite ends of the Bundesliga, but after two games, Elversberg are two points ahead of Bayern.

Elversberg are the best story in European soccer so far this season. They opened with a remarkable 3-2 victory over 2024 Bundesliga champions Bayer Leverkusen, and backed it up with a 4-3 win on the road over Borussia Monchengladbach last time out, complete with a 92nd-minute winner from winger Maurice Krattenmacher. It is a remarkable start and the best thing? They're doing it "the Elversberg way," so says the club's technical director Dr. Josef Welzmüller.

But Bayern are a different proposition. They started the season with a commanding 5-1 win over Stuttgart, but then came unstuck at Schalke, drawing 0-0. Schalke goalkeeper Loris Karius put in a performance for the ages to frustrate a much-rotated Bayern side, with striker Harry Kane introduced in the second half. Bayern will head to Elversberg as overwhelming favourites, but the hosts will fancy their chances of pulling off yet another monumental victory. Bayern played Thursday evening against BodÚ/Glimt, while Elversberg have enjoyed an entire week to plot their masterplan.

MY PREDICTION: Elversberg 3-3 Bayern Munich. Without meaning to sit on the fence, you can see this ending a draw. Elversberg will stick with their all-out attacking style and should score at least one, while Thursday's Champions League match will still be heavy in Bayern's legs. This will finish 3-3.

Can Chelsea kick-start their season?

Manchester United vs. Chelsea

Women's Super League, Matchday 2

Kickoff: Sunday, 7 a.m. ET / 12 p.m. BST

Both teams will wish they could play their opening game again. Manchester United were dismal on the road at the big-spending London City Lionesses, while Chelsea fluffed their lines at home to Aston Villa, drawing 1-1.

United are getting used to life under new boss Eva Olid, but they made a poor start in Bromley. They managed just one shot on target, which came in the 99th minute in the form of a consolation goal from midfielder Simi Awujo after being comprehensively outplayed by London City as Alexia Putellas' crew won 2-1. There's plenty for United to work on.

United playmaker Ella Toone had just seven touches of the ball against London City, which goes some way to explaining how they mustered so little a threat in front of goal. United also looked uncertain at the back and should have lost by more. Olid feels it's a mental block holding United back, but regardless, her promises of attacking football seem a world off materialising.

Over at Chelsea, they saw plenty of departures over the summer and started the new campaign with that draw at Stamford Bridge to Villa. Forward Lauren James scored a typically eye-catching goal, but Chelsea had 34 shots on goal, with just eight on target. They were far too wasteful. Chelsea secured the League Cup last season, but are desperate to regain their WSL crown in what is a squad far more in Sonia Bompastor's image than the two previous seasons. Defender Katie McCabe said post-match Chelsea won't panic after dropping points in their opener, but they will be desperate to bounce back this weekend.

PREDICTION: Manchester United 1-2 Chelsea. Chelsea will have too much for United, but I expect to see an improved showing from Olid's team.

Will Mourinho's Madrid find some momentum?

Real Madrid vs. Rayo Vallecano

LaLiga, Matchday 4

Kickoff: Saturday, 3 p.m. ET / 9 p.m. CEST

After losing 1-0 to Real Betis last weekend -- the first defeat of Jose Mourinho's return to Real Madrid -- they snuck past Inter Milan midweek. However, the 2-1 scoreline didn't tell the whole story: Inter were on top in the first half but still went into the break 2-0 down due to self-inflicted mistakes. Inter got the consolation late on to make things a little nervier for Madrid than they'd have wanted, but Real Madrid -- without Arda Güler and Bernardo Silva -- still came away with the victory.

That match saw Yan Diomande feature on the bench. It's been a slow start in Madrid for the new £120 million signing as he finds his feet. This could be a good occasion for him to stretch his legs, but Real Madrid will be demanding a statement performance after the last round defeat to Real Betis. Kylian Mbappé was back to his usual self against Inter after a tricky match with Betis in which he missed a penalty.

Mbappé and Thibaut Courtois -- along with Güler -- have been Madrid's standout players so far this season, but you sense it needs a far more collective showing in the all-Madrid affair this weekend to illustrate proof of progress in the Mourinho era.

Rayo Vallecano -- last season's Conference League finalists -- have started their campaign with a 1-1 draw against Alaves, a 5-2 defeat to Barcelona and then a 3-2 victory over Racing Santander where they came back from a goal down twice to win. Rayo finished that match with nine men after both Fran Pérez and Jorge de Frutos were sent off, but had Sergio Camello's two goals to thank for helping them to their victory. With Atlético Madrid looming on the horizon on Sept. 20, the onus is on Madrid to find some momentum.

PREDICTION: Real Madrid 3-0 Rayo Vallecano. Mourinho's side will have too much for their neighbours.

Does PSG's wait for a win end here?

Brest vs. Paris Saint-Germain

Ligue 1, Matchday 4

Kickoff: Sunday, 2.45 p.m. ET / 8.45 p.m. CEST

It's an intriguing weekend in Ligue 1. Keep an eye on the outcome in Paris, which will stage a third vs. second clash between Liam Rosenior's Paris FC and Paulo Fonseca's Lyon. AS Monaco are also worth watching as the only team with three wins from three travel to BlueCo's Strasbourg on Saturday, but PSG's fortunes will be where the focus is this weekend.

Though they got a comfortable 6-1 victory versus Slovan Bratislava, they have been underwhelming domestically, having already surrendered the Trophée des Champions to Lens. In Ligue 1, they have played three matches, drawing twice and losing last weekend, 2-1 at home to Monaco. It's been their worst start to a Ligue 1 season under manager Luis Enrique, and he's spent his week telling his players to forget what they've done in the past, and focus on delivering in the present.

A trip to Brest won't be an easy task. They're undefeated in the league this season with two draws and a win but PSG, complete with their 10 Ballon d'Or nominees and that morale-boosting waltz in midweek, will look to get their season finally off and running come Sunday.

PREDICTION: Brest 2-2 PSG. The wait for PSG's first league win of the season will continue for another week.

Can Spurs start to prove the summer wasn't a disaster?

Tottenham Hotspur vs. Everton

Premier League, Matchday 4

Kickoff: Saturday, 12.30 p.m. ET / 5.30 p.m. BST

After a summer outlay in the region of £330 million, Tottenham are yet to score in the Premier League this season -- one of three teams in the England's top tier with such a record. It's far from ideal, and the pressure is mounting on Spurs to pick up some form and show signs of life that it won't be yet another season spent scrapping at the foot of the table.

Memories of Mauricio Pochettino's reign came back to the fore this week as he told assembled media Chelsea should've had their 2017 Premier League title stripped from their grasp and handed to Spurs. Those days feel like they are from another century.

Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi said his forwards need to make better decisions after their 0-0 draw with Nottingham Forest, and it's been another week of unwanted distractions, with the news that on-loan winger Mykhailo Mudryk faces months on the sideline through injury.

Life hasn't been easy for Everton, either. Manager David Moyes is doing an admirable job with a streamlined squad after missing out on United States striker Folarin Balogun on transfer deadline day. Fans are unimpressed with their summer's activity in the transfer market, but one signing did make an early impact, with midfielder Ainsley Maitland-Niles scoring that late equaliser against Manchester United.

PREDICTION: Tottenham Hotspur 2-1 Everton. This match is between two highly taut sides, but Spurs have to come good eventually.

Italy

Lazio vs. AC Milan

Serie A, Matchday 4

Kickoff: Saturday, 12 p.m. ET / 6 p.m. CEST

Before we get to this match between faultless Lazio and AC Milan, spare a thought for Fiorentina's week. After just three matches and a summer transfer spend of €164 million, they dismissed manager Fabio Grosso this week, replacing him with their former coach Paolo Vanoli. Expectations are high at La Viola, and they're not risking anything after that summer of largesse -- a return of zero points, one goal and nine conceded is not what they planned. They travel to Venezia, who are also yet to pick up a point, where both sides will be scrapping for something (anything) and it should be a proper arm-wrestle in The Floating City.

But back to Lazio. There are three teams with a perfect start to the season in Italy: AS Roma, Internazionale and Lazio are all three from three. Roma travel to Torino on Monday while Inter host Udinese. So it's Lazio's match against AC Milan that should be at the forefront of Serie A's focus this weekend.

Lazio started their season with a 1-0 win at Bologna, then defeated Genoa 1-0 and edged past Udinese 2-1 last week. It's all been by the slimmest possible margins, but Milan will provide an altogether sterner test. One man who'll be looking forward to that challenge is Lazio manager Gennaro Gattuso, himself a Milan legend and former manager. He's got the best out of Davide Frattesi this season, but Gattuso said after the Udinese win that he is yet to fully enjoy their impressive start to the campaign as he's forever on edge, waiting for the next complicated situation.

Ruben Amorim's AC Milan team have defeated Torino, Venezia and drawn with Juventus. They've gone through a summer of wholescale change in their squad, with familiar faces departing, and Amorim is still fine-tuning his team, especially in attack where it hasn't clicked yet.

Amorim is still looking for a long-term answer to the No.10 conundrum. They struggled to create chances against Juventus last weekend and will need things to click if they're to get anything off Lazio.

PREDICTION: Lazio 2-1 AC Milan. Lazio will go four from four with AC Milan experiencing more uncertainty up front.

Can Wrexham cause a Championship upset?

West Ham United vs. Wrexham

Championship, Matchday 7

Kickoff: Friday, 3 p.m. ET / 8 p.m. BST

After a slightly shaky start to life in the Championship with a draw at Burnley and loss at home to Charlton, West Ham are slowly finding their rhythm. Winger Jarrod Bowen, of course, is at the forefront of everything they're doing well, and wins over Wolves and Derby have them second in the Championship.

Wrexham's season hasn't started as well. They lie in 14th with four frustrating draws from six matches. A win over Millwall in matchday five looked to have kick-started their season, but then came the 1-1 draw at home to Burnley on Tuesday. Manager Phil Parkinson called for calm after that latest draw with Wrexham struggling to turn attacking possession and glimpses of opportunity into clearcut chances and goals. That's been the story of their season so far.

Elsewhere this weekend, Swansea-Burnley should be entertaining with Vitor Matos' side playing some wondrous football down in south Wales while Southampton's match against the impressive Bristol City is also worth keeping an eye on. And there's also the match between table-topping West Brom and fourth-placed QPR. The Championship always delivers.

PREDICTION: West Ham 2-0 Wrexham. Bowen will inspire West Ham to more points at home.

stories.headline: 'The most risky on the calendar': F1 drivers react to 'crazy' Madring layout ahead of Spanish Grand Prix
stories.summary: Formula 1 drivers have predicted multiple crashes and red flags at this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix after getting their first glimpse of the new Madring circuit.
stories.body:
MADRID -- Formula 1 drivers have predicted multiple crashes and red flags at this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix after getting their first glimpse of the new Madring circuit.

The hybrid street circuit based around Madrid's IFEMA exhibition centre has already caught the attention of a number of drivers after they completed laps in the virtual world on their team's simulators in the build-up to the race weekend.

The combination of high-speed corners -- including the 24-degree banked Turn 12, named La Monumental -- unforgiving walls, and curved braking zones presents one of the more unusual challenges on the F1 calendar.

Questions were raised about the layout of the circuit after a recent two-day Formula 3 test resulted in 19 red flags due to crashes and incidents.

Mercedes driver George Russell was initially shocked by that statistic, but then he drove a lap of the Madring on his team's simulator.

"I heard about the 19 red flags in F3 and I was a bit surprised," he said. "And then, after I drove it on the sim, I was surprised there were only 19 red flags. So, it's a crazy circuit.

"I would put it, arguably, as the most risky circuit of the whole calendar, because you have real high-speed corners, sort of Jeddah-esque. The walls are very close. There's no margin for error.

"But then, you have other corners that are quite like Baku, where you're coming from a high speed into a slow braking zone. You're braking and turning at the same time.

"So, locking tyres is going to be easy. If you're not coping, you'll be straight in the wall.

"I think it's going to be really challenging for us as drivers. The race is going to be challenging to overtake. So, on the whole, it's not an easy one."

- Spanish Grand Prix: Everything you need to know about F1's brand-new Madring

- George Russell needs 'luck' on his side to beat Kimi Antonelli and win world championship

- Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc held face-to-face talks after Monza woes: 'It's healthy'

Pierre Gasly expects the Madring's reputation for session-stopping crashes to continue into the F1 race weekend after he hit a number of the walls during his session in Alpine's simulator.

"I'll put my money on the red flag, that's for sure. Driving-wise, I must say in the sim it was very enjoyable and very exciting.

"I got a good read and feel of pretty much every single wall at every single corner, so I should know what to do and what not to do.

"I expect a very tricky track, challenging for us, which makes it good because you can always aim to do a bit more difference driving-wise. But again, it's a type of track a bit like Monaco, where I think if you do a slight mistake, it can have big consequences straight away, so it's about how you can reward every single braking zone and the speed that you carry through the corners.

"I must say it's exciting, but at the same time I think it's going to be quite a disruptive weekend, how easy it will be to have a crash."

One concern raised by Williams driver Alex Albon on Thursday was the amount of blind corners around the circuit.

The exit of the high-speed La Monumental has already been noted as a section of track where speeds are high and visibility into the next corner is limited.

"It's an interesting track, there's a lot of high speed corners, a lot of blind corners -- it gives me vibes of Macau [the famous street F3 street circuit], but more for an F1 track," Albon said.

"It's a little bit concerning, the blind spots in some of the corners, like if there is a car that's stopped on the other side of the corner, I hope they're just quick on the VSCs [Virtual Safety Cars] and the red flags. Inevitably there are going to be a few crashes this weekend."

Albon also raised concerns about the difficulty of overtaking into some of the braking zones, which are curved into Turn 5, Turn 8 and Turn 17.

"I wish they did something a bit different with the braking zones and not having them too much angled," he added. "You've got a lot of combined corners, which just thinking of overtaking on Sunday, it feels like it's quite easy to defend. You just put the car in the middle of the track and you're not going to get a car that's going to go past you.

"That just means that it will be more of a [battery] deployment overtake than a braking overtake. But yeah, it will be challenging."

Albon also predicted there would be a temptation to take extra risks into the Turn 5 and 6 chicane in qualifying to gain lap time.

"I mean that Turn 5, 6, I hope there's a rhythm to it and it's actually not that bad, but I think there's an angle there that you're going to just send it," he said.

"And if you get through the other side, you're going to be two or three tenths [of a second] quicker. And if you don't want to take that risk, you lose out on those few tenths."

stories.headline: Fantasy hockey breakout forwards: Why Quinn, Coronato should take the next step
stories.summary: Sean breaks down which fantasy hockey forwards have the right conditions to break out this season.
stories.body:
Every fantasy draft turns on a breakout or two -- the player you reach for a round early because you're convinced this is the year it finally clicks. Hit on one and you've got a star at a role-player price. The catch is that "convinced" usually comes down to a hot preseason, a shiny new linemate, or a highlight that lodged in your brain in April.

So instead of guessing who looks ready, I went the other way. I pulled every forward who has actually broken out since 2009-10 and asked what they had in common at the moment it happened, what was true when the breakout happened.

Two things carry more signal than you'd expect: how old a player was, and how many NHL games he already had under him. Break out much younger and you're just betting on talent; much older and you're chasing an outlier that barely happens. There's a window, and it's narrower than the eye test would ever guess.

Here's the quick version of what I'm calling "ready":

The median fantasy points per game (FPPG) across the 1,700 individual top-100 forward seasons since 2009-10 is 1.90, and that's the bar we set for a breakout.

Using all game logs since the 2009-10 season, there are 299 forwards that have made more than one appearance among the top 100 for fantasy scoring. This purposefully excludes any one-time flukes.

Of those 299 forwards, 177 made their debut in 2009-10 or later, meaning we have complete game logs for their entire career.

Of those 177 forwards, 124 eventually held a rolling 41-game FPPG average above 1.90 for at least 41 consecutive games -- a half-season at that pace at minimum, and often longer.

The average age those 124 forwards had reached when that breakout run began was 24 years, 74 days (with the majority doing it between 21 years, 303 days and 26 years, 88 days).

The average experience those 124 forwards had when that run began was 250 games played (with the majority doing it between 142 and 399).

So those are the coordinates. What follows are the forwards sitting inside that window right now who haven't gotten there yet -- because a player who's already banked a top-100 season isn't a breakout, he's a known quantity. These are the ones the math says are due.

More: Sign up for free | Rankings | Projections | League types

The breakouts

Ridly Greig, C, Ottawa Senators (24.1 years old, 1.24 FPPG in 247 games played): Admittedly, Greig isn't my first choice from the list of qualified players, but he's listed first because he is almost exactly the breakout age and experience. He's also going to find himself with a regular top-six role based on the Sens' current depth chart.

Jack Quinn, RW, Buffalo Sabres (25.0 years old, 1.27 FPPG in 260 games played): There are a few different configurations that could play out for the Sabres' scoring lines, but Quinn is firmly in the mix to be a part of them on the wings. There is even a conceivable path here that lands him with top power-play time if he can take the next step.

Matt Coronato, RW, Calgary Flames (23.8 years old, 1.28 FPPG in 192 games played): Has a door been this wide open for young prospects to take the leap before? The Flames' teardown has left them with no choice but to thrust players like Coronato into the limelight. Just watch out for that plus-minus if your custom league still uses it.

Bobby Brink, RW, Minnesota Wild (25.2 years old, 1.15 FPPG in 214 games played): Brink was on his way to a 20-goal season with the Flyers in limited ice time, before the trade to the Wild further cut into his opportunities. Now, Minnesota has some flexibility for new faces to earn key roles and Brink will be in the mix.

Logan Stankoven, C, Carolina Hurricanes (23.5 years old, 1.27 FPPG in 183 games played): The Stanley Cup playoffs were a coming out party for Stankoven, who could have earned himself a Conn Smythe Trophy if Jordan Staal's goals weren't more timely. His line with Jackson Blake and Taylor Hall should hit the ground running in the regular season.

Egor Chinakhov, RW, Pittsburgh Penguins (25.6 years old, 1.19 FPPG in 247 games played): Remember the key breakout threshold we set was high, at 1.90 FPPG. Well, Chinkhov had 1.88 FPPG over the final 43 games of the season after the trade to the Penguins. He essentially already broke out, even if the math didn't quite catch it on a technicality.

Mackie Samoskevich, LW, Seattle Kraken (23.8 years old, 1.23 FPPG in 156 games played): Seattle spent a first-round pick to spring him from Florida's forward logjam, specifically to turn loose his shooter's mentality on a scoring line, likely alongside Shane Wright. He lived among the league leaders in shots per 60 (64th among forwards with at least 100 minutes) on limited Panthers ice time; give him the minutes and the counting stats follow.

Mavrik Bourque, C, Nashville Predators (24.6 years old, 1.06 FPPG in 156 games played): Nashville gave him $33 million and a projected second-line center job -- a massive linemate upgrade for a guy who broke out for 20 goals buried in Dallas' bottom six.

Connor McMichael, C, St. Louis Blues (25.6 years old, 1.21 FPPG in 315 games played): The Jordan Kyrou trade sent him to St. Louis, and his 26-goal, 57-point 2024-25 is the reminder of his top-six ceiling. Just note the Blues also added Mason McTavish down the middle, so McMichael may shuffle between center and wing. The minutes stay top-six, the exact role won't.

Emil Heineman, LW, New York Islanders (24.8 years old, 1.29 FPPG in 148 games played): Riding Bo Horvat's wing, Heineman busted out for 22 goals against just nine assists -- a lopsided line that pegs him as a finisher, not a facilitator. If he holds that top-line spot the goals are real, but treat him as a goals-and-hits multi-category piece and keep the points expectations in check.

Jackson Blake, RW, Carolina Hurricanes (23.1 years old, 1.25 FPPG in 162 games played): Blake closed the playoffs on Carolina's most dangerous line, flanking Stankoven and Hall for a plus-30 across 19 games. That trio should open the year intact on a Cup contender, making the 23-year-old a cheap ticket into one of the league's better even-strength units.

Shane Wright, C, Seattle Kraken (22.7 years old, 1.31 FPPG in 169 games played): We've been penciling in a Wright breakout since draft night, and the pedigree has cashed exactly zero of those checks so far. The difference this time isn't the talent, it's that he's finally banked enough NHL games to be sitting right in the breakout window, with a top-six role that's his to lose.

Marco Kasper, C, Detroit Red Wings (22.4 years old, 1.25 FPPG in 159 games played): Kasper's sophomore crash to nine goals on a 6.9 shooting percentage screams undervalued, especially now that he's healthy after gutting through a knee injury. The swing factor is Dylan Larkin, as a trade vaults Kasper into a top-six role where the shooting luck corrects. If Larkin stays, he's more of a late-round dart.

Frank Nazar, C, Chicago Blackhawks (22.6 years old, 1.43 FPPG in 122 games played): With Connor Bedard shelved into November following shoulder surgery, Nazar will be leaned on in the early season. He buried only 15 of 138 shots last season, so positive regression is coming, and the Bedard-less minutes are his runway to cash in before the role tightens up.

Test out your strategies with the ESPN Mock Draft Lobby.

You again?

A few players were highlighted for this same list last season, but are still in the wheelhouse for a breakout. It's never too late.

Luke Evangelista, RW, New Jersey Devils (24.5 years old, 1.18 FPPG in 253 games played): Surprising late offseason trade to the Devils aside, Evangelista was making this list regardless. He has the skills and budding experience to break through as a fantasy-relevant winger. He's a lock for an opportunity alongside either Nico Hischier or Jack Hughes, which is arguably more enticing than the same top-six chances in Nashville.

Kent Johnson, LW, Columbus Blue Jackets (23.9 years old, 1.14 FPPG in 274 games played): Johnson already flashed the ceiling -- 57 points in 2024-25 -- before a shoulder injury and a career-worst 6.1 shooting percentage buried the followup. But a breakout absolutely requires him to beat out Valeri Nichushkin and/or Conor Garland for the top power-play unit.

Cole Perfetti, LW, Winnipeg Jets (24.7 years old, 1.28 FPPG in 290 games played): We keep waiting on the power-play leap, and Perfetti keeps getting stranded on the wrong unit, with just six power-play points last season despite career-high man-advantage minutes. He's shown 50-point ability, so if Winnipeg finally hands him a true PP1 look behind Kyle Connor and Mark Scheifele, the breakout follows; until then he's a late-round bet on that door opening.

Tyson Foerster, RW, Philadelphia Flyers (24.6 years old, 1.54 FPPG in 195 games played): Foerster carries the highest floor in this tier, thanks to an elite shot and a top-six role with Trevor Zegras plus PP1 time. A November surgery wiped out most of his 2025-26, but he'd banked 13 goals in 29 games before it, and with a healthy runway for once, the 30-goal season people keep projecting becomes the base case.

Mason McTavish, C, St. Louis Blues (23.6 years old, 1.46 FPPG in 304 games played): The former No. 3 pick finally gets a change of scenery in St. Louis, where a projected second-line center job behind Robert Thomas could unlock the offense that stalled in Anaheim. His 2025-26 (41 points in 75 games) underwhelmed, but he's only 23 with real pedigree.

stories.headline: How do the WNBA playoffs work? Dates, format and more
stories.summary: The 2026 WNBA playoffs begins on Sept. 27. Learn more about postseason dates, rules, and stats now.
stories.body:
Led by Paige Bueckers, the Dallas Wings clinched the eighth and final spot in the 2026 WNBA playoffs. Dallas joined the Washington Mystics, New York Liberty, Atlanta Dream, Indiana Fever, Golden State Valkyries, Las Vegas Aces and Minnesota Lynx on the list of teams that earned a postseason berth.

Check out key facts about the 2026 WNBA postseason below:

When do the WNBA playoffs begin?
The WNBA playoffs begin Sept. 27 and will run through the end of September and into late-October.

How do the WNBA playoffs work?
The top eight teams in the WNBA standings at the end of the regular season qualify for the playoffs. The teams are seeded based on their records, so the club with the best record earns the No. 1 seed, and the team with the eighth-best record is the No. 8 seed.

The playoffs are structured like a traditional eight-team bracket. The top seed hosts the No. 8 seed, the No. 2 seed hosts the seventh seed, the No. 3 seed hosts the sixth seed, and the fourth seed hosts the fifth seed.

The first round features four best-of-three series, with the winners advancing to the semifinals. The semifinals consist of two best-of-five series. The winner of each semifinal advances to the WNBA Finals.

The 2026 WNBA Finals will be a best-of-seven series for the second time in league history. The series will have a 2-2-1-1-1 structure in which the higher seed hosts Games 1, 2, 5 and 7, and its opponent hosts Games 3, 4 and 6. The first team to win four games in the series is the 2026 WNBA champion.

Which team won the 2025 WNBA championship?
The Aces swept the Phoenix Mercury 4-0 in the 2025 WNBA Finals to win their third WNBA championship in four years. A'ja Wilson was named Finals MVP for the second time in her career (2023).

Who won the past five WNBA championships?

2025: Las Vegas Aces
2024: New York Liberty
2023: Las Vegas Aces
2022: Las Vegas Aces
2021: Chicago Sky

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little ealier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Thursday, Sept. 10

Hogan set to join Pies

GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: Messi tracker: Goals, assists, key moments in 2026
stories.summary: ESPN provides game-by-game analysis of Lionel Messi's performances for Inter Miami and Argentina.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi will aim for more success in 2026. His Inter Miami side captured its first MLS Cup title last season and will look to defend it -- and add further silverware too -- in its first season at Nu Stadium, the club's new home.

Messi also captained Argentina as they fell just one step short of defending their FIFA World Cup crown, losing 1-0 in extra time to Spain in the final of what could be his last tournament.

As the 39-year-old continues to feature for both club and country, ESPN will track his performances game-by-game, providing stats and analysis each time he pulls on a Herons or Albiceleste jersey.

Messi's 2026 tally:

Games played: 35
Goals: 31
Assists: 14

Sep. 9: Chicago Fire 1-1 Inter Miami

Two or Europe's greatest club players took center stage in one of the United States' most iconic American football stadiums on Wednesday -- and a record crowd came out to watch.

Ex-Bayern Munich and Barcelona star Robert Lewandowski scored a trademark acrobatic goal in the 10th minute to give the Fire an early lead at the NFL home of the Chicago Bears.

But Inter Miami drew level shortly after halftime when Casemiro, another of the game's stars with a long history of playing in Europe before moving to MLS, headed home a Messi cross from a corner kick to make it 1-1.

The assist was Messi's league-leading 13th of the season. He also has league 18 goals and is the first player in MLS history with 30-plus goal contributions in three separate seasons.

Sep. 5: Inter Miami 2-2 Atlanta United
Messi was not as effective as he was in the previous matchup, but he did get an assist for Casemiro's opening goal. However, his team was unable to win as they had to settle for a point in a 2-2 draw.

August 29: Inter Miami 7-1 CF Montréal

Fans were treated to a Messi masterclass on Saturday as the Argentine magician registered four goals and an assist to help Miami to a club-record 7-1 victory over CF Montréal.

Messi scored with a deflected free kick in the 40th minute before netting after a stunning solo run in the 52nd. After supplying an assist to Luis Suárez, the 39-year-old then completed his hat trick and with a delicate chip over the goalkeeper with seven minutes of regulation time remaining.

He wasn't done yet.

Deep into stoppage time, Messi lined up a free kick and dispatched it with trademark precision into the top corner of the net. Legendary stuff.

August 22: Inter Miami 2-1 Toronto FC

Messi's 14th MLS goal of the season wasn't enough to prevent Inter Miami from slumping to their fourth loss in their last five games, losing 2-1 to Toronto FC at Nu Stadium on Saturday.

Messi found the net with a first-time finish from a Rodrigo De Paul through-ball with eight minutes remaining, but the home side's late rally fell short of salvaging a much-needed draw to bolster the Herons' pursuit of first-placed Nashville SC in the Eastern Conference.

August 19: Inter Miami 2-2 Philadelphia Union

Messi is back scoring goals, but unfortunately, his Miami side is not back to winning ways. The Argentine scored Miami's second goal of the night as both teams finished with 10 men. Miami are now winless in their last four matches.

August 15: Nashville SC 4-1 Inter Miami
It was not the best night for Messi in Tennessee. The Argentine missed yet another penalty -- his third straight for club and country -- and they suffered a heavy 4-1 loss to their Eastern Conference rivals. However, he did get an assist for Telasco Segovia's equalizer at halftime before Miami lost control in the second half.

August 12: Inter Miami 2-3 Club León
Just days after the passing of his father, Messi came off the bench in the second half to try to help Miami continue in the Leagues Cup after they were leading 1-0. However, it ended in a 3-2 loss which saw them eliminated in the league phase after a second straight loss, coming off defeat to Monterrey last weekend with Messi away at the memorial for his father.

August 5: Inter Miami 4-2 Atlético de San Luis

Lionel Messi made his first start for Inter Miami since returning from the World Cup and picked up right where he left off, scoring a stellar pair of goals to guide his team to a come-from-behind 4-2 rout of Atlético de San Luis in its first game of the 2026 Leagues Cup.

Messi's first goal was an exquisite volley, redirecting Noah Allen's cross from the left flank while running at full speed. Miami's third goal of the opening half -- and Messi's second on the night -- came on the back of some intricate buildup play with Allen once again setting up his team captain, this time in the center of the area where he tiptoed through two defenders and buried a close-range strike past Andrés Sánchez.

The goal made Messi the all-time leading scorer in Leagues Cup history with 14, one ahead of LAFC's Denis Bouanga since the expanded competition began in 2023.

August 1: Inter Miami 2-2 Columbus Crew
Messi made his return to action for Inter Miami on Saturday, 13 days after tasting defeat with Argentina in the World Cup final. The Miami talisman started on the substitutes' bench before being introduced in the 53rd minute of the Herons' 2-2 draw with the Columbus Crew at Nu Stadium in Miami.

July 19: Spain 1-0 AET Argentina

Sunday proved to be a bridge too far for both Messi and Argentina, falling in extra time to Spain in the World Cup final.

With La Roja controlling the match basically from start to finish -- Argentina didn't register a shot on target during regulation time -- Messi had few opportunities to impact the game. Indeed, the 39-year-old was given a 3/10 in ESPN's post-match player ratings.

Still, as Mark Ogden points out, the 2026 tournament was a memorable one for Messi and cemented his status as the GOAT, if it were ever in doubt.

July 15: England 1-2 Argentina
Messi made another statement in his 205th appearance for Argentina, this time in his first-ever match against England in a World Cup semifinal. With so much at stake for both nations, Messi once again proved decisive despite not getting on the scoresheet.

He first provided the assist for Enzo Fernández's superb strike to level the match in the second half before delivering a pinpoint cross for Lautaro Martínez's headed winner, sending the reigning champions into yet another World Cup final after another dramatic encounter.

Messi has now recorded either a goal or an assist in all seven of Argentina's matches at this World Cup, and he will have the opportunity to lift the trophy for a second time when Argentina face Spain in Sunday's final in New Jersey.

July 11: Argentina 3-1 Switzerland
It was a relatively quiet night by Messi's standards as his goalscoring streak came to an end, but his influence on the match stayed the same. He set up Alexis Mac Allister's opening goal for Argentina against Switzerland, and although the match went to extra time, the defending champions won 3-1 thanks to two late goals in the second half of extra time.

Messi's quest to retain the World Cup now continues into the semifinals, where Argentina will face England for the first time in over 20 years. The clash in Atlanta -- one of international soccer's most storied rivalries -- will decide a spot in the final.

July 7: Argentina 3-2 Egypt
It was another dramatic outing for Messi and Argentina, who rallied from a 2-0 deficit to defeat Egypt 3-2 in Atlanta and book their place in the World Cup quarterfinals. As is so often the case, Messi was at the center of the action. Minutes after Egypt opened the scoring, he missed another penalty, but he quickly made amends by setting up Cristian Romero for Argentina's first goal. Messi then scored the equalizer -- his eighth goal of the tournament -- before Enzo Fernández completed the comeback with the winner. Argentina will now face Switzerland in Kansas City for a place in the semifinals.

July 3: Argentina 3-2 Cape Verde
Messi suffered a major scare in Miami Gardens on Friday evening in the round of 32, but it ultimately ended well for Argentina. He opened the scoring with his seventh goal of the tournament, extending his World Cup tally to 20 goals while finding the net in a record eighth consecutive World Cup match. Cape Verde twice fought back -- once in the second half and again in extra time -- but the world champions eventually prevailed 3-2 after extra time to book a meeting in the round of 16 with Egypt.

June 27: Jordan 1-3 Argentina
Messi didn't play the full 90 minutes in Argentina's 3-1 win over an already-eliminated Jordan, but he still made his mark during a 30-minute cameo in Texas. The 39-year-old scored a free kick for his sixth goal of the tournament and his 19th career World Cup goal, becoming the first player ever to score in seven consecutive World Cup matches. Even at 39, he's still got it.

June 22: Argentina 2-0 Austria
Another chapter in an already unparalleled career. Lionel Messi scored twice in Argentina's 2-0 win over Austria to help his team qualify for the round of 32 and become the outright leading goalscorer in men's and women's FIFA World Cup history with 18 goals. After missing an early penalty, he responded by breaking Miroslav Klose's 12-year-old record and then added a second late on to break Marta's record. All just two days before turning 39.

June 16: Argentina 3-0 Algeria
In his 200th appearance for Argentina and sixth World Cup, Lionel Messi sent a message to the world just days before his 39th birthday: he still has it. His first-ever World Cup hat trick powered Argentina to victory in their group-stage opener, while his 16th tournament goal saw him draw level with Miroslav Klose for the most goals in World Cup history.

June 9: Argentina 3-0 Iceland

Messi, working his way back from muscle fatigue ahead of the start of the World Cup, came on in the 70th minute of a pre-tournament friendly in Auburn, Alabama and scored from the penalty spot right afterward.

It was Messi's 911th career goal for club and country and 117th goal for Argentina and made him the oldest scorer in the country's soccer history.

May 24: Inter Miami 6-4 Philadelphia Union

Messi registered two assists in a scintillating performance against Philadelphia on Sunday but, unfortunately, no one was focused on results come the end of the game.

That's because, in the very last game before the World Cup, Messi left the field in the 73rd minute and headed straight to the locker room after grabbing his left thigh.

Now, supporters around the world are holding their collective breath while they wait and see if the injury has scuppered the 38-year-old's chance of appearing at a sixth World Cup.

May 13: FC Cincinnati 3-5 Inter Miami

Two goals and one assist marked yet another spectacular contribution from Miami superstar Messi on Wednesday. The Argentine magician was instrumental as the Herons fought back from 3-2 down to eventually beat Cincinnati 5-3 at TQL Stadium in Ohio.

May 9: Toronto FC 2-4 Inter Miami

It was a day of star power. Not only were Rodrigo De Paul, Luis Suárez and Sergio Reguilón all on the score sheet for the Herons, so was Messi -- and he added a pair of assists, too.

While Miami has yet to taste victory at its new home, it continues to take care of business on the road. Saturday's win in Toronto extended the club's unbeaten record away from home in 2026 to seven games, picking up six wins and one draw in the first few months of the season.

May 2: Inter Miami 3-4 Orlando City

Messi notched a goal and an assist on Saturday in what ended up being an astonishing collapse for Inter Miami at Nu Stadium.

The Herons were leading 3-0 after Messi's classy 33rd-minute strike, but gifted the visitors four goals -- including a Martín Ojeda hat trick -- to once again miss out on a victory at their new home ground. Orlando's comeback from three goals down marks only the third time in MLS history that a team has claimed all three points after trailing by three or more goals.

As for Messi's Miami, only twice has an MLS team had a longer winless run -- now up to four for the Herons -- to open up a new stadium.

April 25: Inter Miami 1-1 New England Revolution
Messi again failed to get on the scoresheet as Miami put in a fatigued second-half performance that saw them come from a goal down against New England. It was another draw -- and another game without a win at their new home, Nu Stadium.

April 22: Real Salt Lake 0-2 Inter Miami
No goals or assists from Messi as Miami visited America First Field on Wednesday, but the fans did get treated to sumptuous strikes nonetheless.

Rodrigo De Paul's opener in the 80th-minute was stunning curler from outside the box and then, almost immediately after the restart, Luis Suarez made it 2-0 with a well-struck volley.

The victory moves Inter Miami into outright second in the MLS Eastern Conference.

April 18: Colorado Rapids 2-3 Inter Miami

Another moment of Messi magic bagged all three points for Inter Miami on Saturday.

With scores level in the 79th minute, the Argentine icon danced his way past a number of Colorado defenders before curling home an outrageous effort into the far corner.

The strike -- Messi's second of the match after converting a penalty in the first half -- helped Miami to their first win under interim coach Guillermo Hoyos.

Hoyos, who had been serving as club's sporting director, took over coaching duties after Javier Mascherano unexpectedly left the club due to personal reasons last week.

April 11: Inter Miami 2-2 Red Bull New York
Miami and Messi are still waiting for a first win at Nu Stadium after a 2-2 draw with Red Bull New York on Saturday night.

Messi didn't register a goal or assist, but did help set up Germán Berterame's second-half strike that gave Inter Miami its first lead at its new home ground, but 17-year-old Adri Mehmeti's first career goal in the 77th minute secured a point for the visitors.

April 4: Inter Miami 2-2 Austin FC
Inter Miami opened Nu Stadium the only way it knows how: With a Messi goal. The No. 10 began the move in trademark style with a left-footed pass to a teammate before moving past a defender and arriving in the box at just the right time to head past goalkeeper Brad Stuver.

March 31: Argentina 5-0 Zambia
It was the last day of the month and perhaps the last game for Messi playing for Argentina playing in his native country, but they put on a show defeating the African side Zambia 5-0. Messi scored the second goal for Lionel Scaloni's side as focus will shift now to Miami until the beginning of the World Cup.

March 27: Argentina 2-1 Mauritania
In his first game for his country in 2026, Messi only played the second half as Argentina won 2-1 against Mauritania at the mythical La Bombonera in Buenos Aires, as the World Cup champions continue to prepare to defend their title this summer in North America.

March 22: NYCFC 2-3 Inter Miami

It was a thrilling encounter in the Bronx, as the Argentine star helped his team to a 3-2 win over NYCFC, which also included another trademark free kick goal, now beginning his course for potentially 1,000 career goals. Only 99 goals left!

March 18: Inter Miami 1-1 Nashville SC

Messi may have made history on Wednesday night, becoming just the second men's player in history to score 900 career goals, but it wasn't enough to seal Miami's progress in the Concacaf Champions Cup.

The Argentina legend found the back of the net in the seventh minute at Chase Stadium, but his strike was cancelled out by Nashville's Cristian Espinoza -- sealing the Herons' tournament exit on the away goals rule.

March 11: Nashville SC 0-0 Inter Miami
A drab night for Messi and Co. in the Concacaf Champions Cup. Plenty of possession but few shots on target mean that the Herons will return to Chase Stadium know a win will be needed to ensure progression.

March 7: D.C. United 1-2 Inter Miami

It was quite an eventful week for Messi. Just days before Miami's match against D.C. United, Messi and the entire squad visited the White House and met President Donald Trump and were eager to put on a show for the sold-out crowd of over 70,000 at Baltimore's M&T Bank Stadium.

And they did just that, with a 2-1 win over D.C. United. Messi, of course, scored Miami's second and is now one goal away from 900 career goals.

March 1: Orlando City 2-4 Inter Miami

Well, that blip didn't last long! Messi and Miami roared back into life with a 4-2 thrashing of Orlando on Sunday thanks to the 38-year-old's wizardry.

Things looked ominous for the Herons after the first 45 minutes, down 2-0 and looking on course to start the MLS season with two bleak losses.

But two goals and an assist from Messi in the second half dragged the visitors back in the game and helped secure Miami their first points of the season.

Feb. 21: LAFC 3-0 Inter Miami
Messi and Miami aimed to start 2026 firing on all cylinders, but it was the hosts who spoiled the defending MLS Cup champions' opener at the LA Coliseum. In front of a sellout crowd of 75,673 -- the second-highest attendance in MLS history -- Miami were outplayed, with LAFC's Denis Bouanga getting a goal and an assist in a convincing home victory.

The main talking point, however, emerged after the final whistle. Messi was initially reported to have gained unauthorized access to the officials' locker room after video circulated showing him near the area. However, it was later reported that no league policy had been violated and Messi was cleared of any wrongdoing. Miami will now turn its attention next weekend against fellow Florida side Orlando City.

stories.headline: 'Swear by it': night ritual key to Dolphin's 96 in row
stories.summary: Dolphins winger Jamayne Isaako will happily be stranded on '99 not out' if it means winning a title at the club where he has not missed a match in four years.
stories.body:
Jamayne Isaako credits nightly saunas as integral to him playing 96 consecutive NRL games for a Dolphins club that he never wanted to leave.

The Melbourne-bound winger will play the Warriors away in Saturday's qualifying final with a goal to play at least 99 consecutive matches for the Dolphins.

"To have played all 96 games in a row is something to be proud of and I would happily take 100. To do that inside four years would be something special," Isaako told AAP.

"I'd be equally happy with 99."

To get to 100, the Dolphins would need to lose against the Warriors and progress to the grand final the long way.

"We will take this week first and worry about that when it comes," Isaako grinned.

Isaako puts his iron man ways down to his nightly sauna ritual.

For a long time he was a regular at recovery centres in the Redcliffe area.

"I ended up buying a sauna of my own, but then I managed be hooked with a company called Nordhaus who sponsored me with a great sauna," he said.

"I do it every night and I swear by it. It plays a big part in keeping me on the field and my body healthy. It helps me sleep as well.

"My ability to stay on the field is a lot to do with my recovery. The things you do off the field contribute to how you perform at training and in games.

"I have prioritised my preparation, which at this level is key."

Isaako is without doubt one of the keys to the Dolphins winning a maiden title. In 2026 he was the NRL's regular season leading points scorer for the third time in his four-year stint at the club and for the fourth time in his career.

This year, his 288 points is his best points return yet, including 21 tries and 102 goals from 121 attempts.

Dolphins training days are intense and don't allow Isaako time to spend a lot of time on his goalkicking craft, so his extras are key.

"So when I have time off I go down to the Albany Creek Crushers and kick goals down there," he said.

"I bump into a whole heap of the public who see me kicking there as well, but if I want to be good at it I have to incorporate in my training schedule."

The 30-year-old New Zealand international s rightly proud of his point-scoring awards.

"You don't do it for the accolades, but being a try-scoring winger and having the goalkicking job, I am grateful to score that many points," he said.

"Throughout the last couple of years we have been a great attacking team and that has helped me get those awards."

Isaako's intent is to leave with a premiership before joining the Storm in 2027.

"There are young players coming through and I couldn't really come to an agreement with the Dolphins," he said.

"I would have loved to have stayed but it wasn't meant to be, I guess.

"I love this club and I love the people. I have created some of my fondest rugby league memories at this club. Playing in the inaugural Dolphins game and being a foundation player is something I will hold dear to my heart forever."

Isaako's partner is from Melbourne, which will make the move south easier.

"She was born and raised there and all her family are still there," he said.

"It will be nice to be close to that support."
